items.p: Say your name and how old you are.
items.pv: Nói tên và tuổi của bạn.
items.m: Hello! My name is Lan. I am eight years old.

items.p: Say your favourite colour and one thing with that colour.
items.pv: Nói màu bạn thích và một đồ vật có màu đó.
items.m: My favourite colour is blue. My bag is blue and my bike is blue too.

items.p: Say who is in your family.
items.pv: Nói gia đình bạn có những ai.
c: Anh chị em hoặc ông bà
u: There are four people in my family
Tôi có một anh / em trai
items.m: There are four people in my family: my mum, my dad, my sister and me.

items.p: Say what pet you have or want, and what it looks like.
items.pv: Nói con vật bạn nuôi (hoặc muốn nuôi) và trông nó thế nào.
items.m: I have a dog. It is small and brown. Its name is Bo.

items.p: Say two foods you like and one food you don't like.
items.pv: Nói hai món bạn thích và một món bạn không thích.
items.m: I like rice and chicken. I don't like fish.

items.p: Say what is in your classroom.
items.pv: Nói trong lớp bạn có những gì.
items.m: In my classroom there is a big board. There are twenty desks and a lot of books.

items.p: Say what rooms are in your house and your favourite room.
items.pv: Nói nhà bạn có những phòng nào và phòng bạn thích nhất.
items.m: My house has a kitchen, a living room and two bedrooms. My favourite room is my bedroom.

items.p: Say two animals you like at the zoo and why.
items.pv: Nói hai con vật bạn thích ở sở thú và vì sao.
items.m: I like monkeys and elephants. Monkeys are funny and elephants are very big.

items.p: Say two things you can do and one thing you can't do.
items.pv: Nói hai việc bạn biết làm và một việc chưa biết làm.
items.m: I can swim and I can ride a bike. I can't play the piano.

items.p: Say your friend's name and what you play together.
items.pv: Nói tên bạn của bạn và hai bạn chơi gì cùng nhau.
items.m: My friend's name is Nam. We play football after school.

items.p: Say what you are wearing today and the colours.
items.pv: Nói hôm nay bạn mặc gì và màu gì.
u: Tôi đang mặc áo phông đỏ
items.m: Today I'm wearing a white T-shirt, black trousers and red shoes.

items.p: Say when your birthday is and what you like to eat on your birthday.
items.pv: Nói sinh nhật bạn vào tháng nào và hôm đó bạn thích ăn gì.
u: Sinh nhật tôi vào tháng Năm
items.m: My birthday is in June. On my birthday I like cake and ice cream.

items.p: Say two toys you have and which one you like best.
items.pv: Nói hai đồ chơi bạn có và bạn thích cái nào nhất.
u: I have a ball and a robot
Tôi có quả bóng và rô-bốt
items.m: I have a ball and a robot. I like my robot best because it can walk.

items.p: Say what the weather is like today and what you can do.
items.pv: Nói hôm nay thời tiết thế nào và bạn có thể làm gì.
u: Tôi có thể chơi ngoài trời
items.m: It's sunny and hot today. I can go to the park and play.

items.p: Say what is in your school bag.
items.pv: Nói trong cặp sách của bạn có gì.
u: In my bag there are three books
Trong cặp tôi có ba quyển sách
một hộp bút màu xanh lá
items.m: In my school bag there are three books, a pencil case and a red ruler.

items.p: Introduce yourself. Say your name, age, where you are from, what you do and one hobby.
items.pv: Giới thiệu bản thân: tên, tuổi, quê, bạn làm gì.
u: In my free time, I like
items.m: Hello! My name is Minh and I'm twenty years old. I'm from Da Nang, but now I live in Hanoi. I'm a student at a university of technology. In my free time, I like playing badminton and listening to music.

items.p: Describe your home. Where is it? How many rooms are there? What is your favourite room?
items.pv: Tả nhà bạn: ở đâu, có mấy phòng, phòng bạn thích nhất.
c: Phòng yêu thích và lý do
items.m: I live in a small house near the market. There are three bedrooms, a kitchen and a living room. My favourite room is the kitchen, because it is warm and my mother cooks delicious food there.

items.p: Talk about your favourite food. What is it? When do you eat it? Who cooks it?
items.pv: Nói về món ăn bạn thích: món gì, khi nào ăn, ai nấu.
c: Ai nấu hoặc bạn mua ở đâu
items.m: My favourite food is pho. I usually eat it for breakfast on Sunday. My father often makes it at home, but sometimes we go to a small restaurant near my school. It is hot and very tasty.

items.p: Talk about your best friend. What is his or her name? How old is he or she? What does he or she look like? What do you do together?
items.pv: Nói về bạn thân: tên, ngoại hình, hai bạn làm gì cùng nhau.
c: Việc hai bạn làm cùng nhau
items.m: My best friend is Hoa. She is nineteen. She is tall and she has long black hair. She is very funny. We often go to the cinema together, and at weekends we ride our bikes around the lake.

items.p: What is the weather like today? What do you like to do in this weather? What is your favourite season?
items.pv: Hôm nay thời tiết thế nào? Bạn thích làm gì khi thời tiết như vậy?
items.m: Today it is cloudy and a little cold. When it is like this, I like to stay at home and read a book with a cup of tea. When it is sunny, I go to the park. My favourite season is autumn.

items.p: Tell me about a holiday you enjoyed. Where did you go? Who did you go with? What did you do there?
items.pv: Kể về một kỳ nghỉ bạn thích: đi đâu, với ai, làm gì.
c: Đi cùng ai, đi bằng gì
items.m: Last summer I went to Phu Quoc with my family. We went there by plane, and it only took one hour. We stayed in a small hotel near the beach. Every day we swam, ate seafood and walked on the beach in the evening. The best part was a boat trip to a small island. I really enjoyed it because the water was so clear and blue.

items.p: Describe a typical day in your life. What do you do in the morning, afternoon and evening? Which part of the day do you like best?
items.pv: Tả một ngày điển hình của bạn và phần nào trong ngày bạn thích nhất.
c: Phần bạn thích nhất và lý do
items.m: I usually get up at half past six and have breakfast with my sister. Then I go to work by motorbike. I work in an office from eight to five. After that, I go to the gym or meet friends. In the evening I cook dinner and watch a series. I like the evening best because I can relax and do what I want.

items.p: Do you like shopping? Where do you usually shop, and what do you buy? Do you prefer shopping online or in shops?
items.pv: Bạn có thích mua sắm không? Thường mua ở đâu, mua gì? Bạn thích mua online hay ở cửa hàng?
c: Bạn có thích mua sắm không

items.p: Some people think life is better in the countryside than in the city. Do you agree? Give reasons and examples, and consider the other point of view.

items.m: In my opinion, it depends on your stage of life, but on the whole I prefer the city. For young people especially, cities offer far more opportunities: better jobs, universities and a wider range of cultural activities. For example, in Ho Chi Minh City I can go to concerts, try food from all over the world and meet people from many backgrounds. Having said that, I understand why many people prefer the countryside. The air is cleaner, life is less stressful and housing is much cheaper. Many of my friends with young children have moved back to their home towns for exactly these reasons. On balance, I'd say the city is better for building a career, but the countryside may be better for raising a family.

Instead of criticising me, he stayed after class twice a week to help me, and he always explained things in several different ways until I understood. What I admire most is his patience. He never made me feel stupid. Thanks to him, I not only passed my exams, but I also learned that being bad at something is not permanent. That idea has helped me in everything I've done since, including learning English.

items.m: One clear advantage of online learning is flexibility. You can study whenever and wherever you like, which is ideal for people who work full-time. It's also usually cheaper, and you can replay lessons as many times as you need. The main drawback is that it's easy to lose motivation when nobody is checking on you. It can also feel quite lonely. In a classroom, by contrast, you can ask questions immediately, practise speaking with other students and get instant feedback from the teacher. Personally, I'd choose a mix of both. I'd use online lessons for grammar and vocabulary, but I'd want a real class for speaking practice, because that's where I need most help.

By the afternoon the sun came out, and the ceremony in the garden was beautiful. My whole family was there, including my grandmother, who had travelled from the countryside. It was memorable because it showed me how a community can turn a disaster into something wonderful.

items.vi: Đại học có nên miễn phí?
items.p: Some people argue that university education should be free for everyone. Discuss the arguments for and against, and give your own view.
items.pv: Có ý kiến cho rằng đại học nên miễn phí cho mọi người. Bàn ý ủng hộ, phản đối và nêu quan điểm.
u: Người ủng hộ lập luận rằng

Một giải pháp dung hoà có thể là
items.m: Proponents argue that free university education is a matter of fairness. Talent is spread evenly across society, but money is not, so charging fees means that many capable young people from poor families never get the chance to study. A more educated population also benefits the whole economy. Critics, however, point out that someone has to pay, and that free tuition often benefits middle-class families most, since their children are more likely to go to university anyway. There is also a risk that universities become underfunded and overcrowded. My own view is that cost should never be the reason a talented student cannot study. A compromise might be to make university free for students from lower-income families, while others repay loans once they earn above a certain salary.

items.vi: Tác động của mạng xã hội
items.p: How has social media changed the way people communicate and form opinions? Is the overall effect positive or negative?
items.pv: Mạng xã hội đã thay đổi cách con người giao tiếp và hình thành quan điểm ra sao? Tác động chung là tích cực hay tiêu cực?
c: Ảnh hưởng tới cách hình thành quan điểm
u: Mạng xã hội đã thay đổi căn bản
items.m: Social media has fundamentally changed how we communicate. We now stay in constant contact with hundreds of people, including many we have never met, and news travels in seconds rather than days. One consequence is that our opinions are increasingly shaped by algorithms that show us content we already agree with. This can create echo chambers, where people rarely encounter opposing views and become more extreme. Misinformation also spreads faster than corrections. That said, social media has undeniable benefits. It has given a voice to people who were previously ignored, helped small businesses reach customers and allowed communities to organise quickly in emergencies. Overall, I'd argue that the effect is mixed, and that it depends largely on how critically we use it.

items.p: Many people say it is increasingly difficult to achieve a healthy work-life balance. Why might this be? What can individuals and employers do about it?
items.pv: Nhiều người nói ngày càng khó cân bằng công việc và cuộc sống. Vì sao? Cá nhân và công ty có thể làm gì?

items.m: There are several reasons for this. Technology means that many of us are reachable at any time, so the working day never truly ends. Economic pressure and job insecurity also push people to work longer hours to prove their value. As a result, stress and burnout have become extremely common, and relationships and health often suffer. On a personal level, people can set clear boundaries, for example by switching off work notifications in the evening and protecting time for exercise and family. Employers, for their part, have a responsibility too. They can discourage emails outside working hours, offer flexible schedules and, most importantly, ensure that managers lead by example, since staff tend to copy what their bosses do rather than what they say.

items.m: I'd argue that it is essential to preserve traditional customs and crafts, not because the past is always better, but because they give communities a sense of identity and continuity. Take, for instance, the pottery village of Bat Trang. Its techniques have been passed down for centuries, and losing them would mean losing knowledge that cannot be recovered. The difficulty, of course, is that young people often see little future in traditional crafts, which tend to be poorly paid compared with factory or office work. Responsibility should be shared between governments, which can provide funding and protect heritage sites, and communities themselves, who can find ways to make traditions relevant today, for example through tourism, design collaborations or online sales.

learn.vi: Lý do: 40% khách hàng mới là người nước ngoài

learn.t: I can see why you're frustrated. When did this start happening?
About two weeks ago. I find out only when the client complains.

learn.t: Why don't the three of us have a short meeting to agree on a process?
I suppose. But what if he gets defensive?

learn.vi: Khuyên tập trung vào quy trình, không đổ lỗi

OK, that makes sense. Can you arrange it?

tests.t: That sounds really stressful. How is it affecting your work?
I have to stay late to finish everything myself.

tests.t: Then it would be worth raising it with the team leader so the work can be shared more fairly.

items.p: "Not all progress is improvement." Discuss this statement with reference to technology, society or the environment.
items.pv: “Không phải tiến bộ nào cũng là cải thiện.” Bàn về nhận định này, liên hệ công nghệ, xã hội hoặc môi trường.
c: Ví dụ tiến bộ có cái giá
u: At first glance, the statement seems
Thoạt nhìn, nhận định có vẻ
It would be simplistic, however, to
Tuy nhiên sẽ là quá đơn giản nếu
Ultimately, the question is not whether … but
Rốt cuộc, câu hỏi không phải là … mà là
items.m: At first glance, the statement seems almost paradoxical, since we tend to use 'progress' as a synonym for improvement. But progress, strictly speaking, simply means movement in a particular direction, and whether that direction is desirable is a separate question. A telling example is the rise of the car. It brought unprecedented freedom of movement, yet it also reshaped our cities around traffic rather than people, contributed heavily to pollution and made many communities dependent on long commutes. It would be simplistic, however, to conclude that progress is therefore suspect. Medicine offers countless advances whose benefits are overwhelmingly clear. Ultimately, the question is not whether we should pursue progress, but whether we are sufficiently honest about its costs, and whether those who bear those costs have any say in the decision.

items.en: The Role of Art in Society
items.vi: Vai trò của nghệ thuật trong xã hội
items.p: Should governments fund the arts, even when there are more urgent needs such as healthcare and housing? Justify your position.
items.pv: Chính phủ có nên tài trợ nghệ thuật khi còn những nhu cầu cấp bách hơn như y tế, nhà ở? Lập luận cho quan điểm của bạn.
c: Lập luận giá trị của nghệ thuật
u: To dismiss the arts as a luxury is to
Coi nghệ thuật là xa xỉ tức là
Tôi sẵn sàng thừa nhận rằng
items.m: I would contend that governments should fund the arts, even in difficult times, although the scale and form of that funding deserve careful thought. To dismiss the arts as a luxury is to misunderstand their role. They are one of the principal ways in which a society reflects on itself, preserves its memory and imagines alternatives. They also have tangible benefits: cultural industries employ large numbers of people, and access to the arts has been linked to improved mental health and educational outcomes. I readily concede that when people lack adequate housing or medical care, those needs must take priority, and that arts funding can sometimes serve elite audiences rather than the public. What matters, then, is not whether to fund the arts, but how: prioritising projects that are genuinely accessible, rooted in communities and open to those who would otherwise be excluded.

items.p: "If you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear." Evaluate this argument about surveillance and privacy.
items.pv: “Không có gì để giấu thì chẳng có gì phải sợ.” Đánh giá lập luận này về giám sát và quyền riêng tư.
c: Nêu và diễn giải lập luận
Thừa nhận lý do giám sát
u: The argument has a superficial appeal, but
Lập luận nghe có lý bề ngoài, nhưng
It rests on the assumption that
Nó dựa trên giả định rằng
This is not to deny that
Điều này không phủ nhận rằng
items.m: The argument has a superficial appeal, but it collapses on closer inspection. It rests on the assumption that privacy matters only to people engaged in wrongdoing, which is plainly false. We close the bathroom door not because we are doing anything illegal, but because certain aspects of life are legitimately our own. Moreover, the argument assumes that those conducting surveillance will always be benevolent and competent, and that the definition of wrongdoing will never change. History suggests otherwise: information gathered for one purpose is frequently used for another. This is not to deny that some surveillance is justified, for example in investigating serious crime, provided it is targeted, proportionate and subject to independent oversight. In short, the question is not whether we have something to hide, but who decides what we must reveal, and with what safeguards.

items.p: How far do you agree that modern societies confuse success with happiness? Draw on personal observation or wider examples.
items.pv: Bạn đồng ý tới đâu rằng xã hội hiện đại nhầm lẫn thành công với hạnh phúc? Dùng quan sát cá nhân hoặc ví dụ rộng hơn.
c: Biểu hiện của sự nhầm lẫn
u: I am broadly in agreement, with one qualification.
Tôi về cơ bản đồng ý, với một điểm dè dặt.
Sự nhầm lẫn này thể hiện ở
Ví dụ tôi từng quan sát thấy
Perhaps the more fruitful question is
Có lẽ câu hỏi đáng bàn hơn là
items.m: I am broadly in agreement, with one qualification. This confusion manifests itself in the way we measure lives: by salary, job title, property and, increasingly, by visibility on social media. These markers are easy to compare and easy to display, which makes them convenient stand-ins for something far harder to assess. I have observed, for instance, friends who achieved every goal their parents set for them and yet describe themselves as exhausted and strangely empty. Research on wellbeing tends to support this impression: beyond a modest level of income, relationships, autonomy and a sense of purpose matter considerably more than further gains in status. My qualification is that success and happiness are not opposites; meaningful achievement can be a profound source of satisfaction. Perhaps the more fruitful question is not whether to pursue success, but whose definition of it we are pursuing.

items.vi: Phỏng vấn xin việc cấp quản lý: câu hỏi khó

learn.t: Thank you for coming. Let's start with a difficult one: what's your greatest weakness?

learn.vi: Thừa nhận đôi khi ôm việc thay vì giao cho người khác
learn.t: I've sometimes found it hard to delegate. I tend to take on too much myself rather than trusting the team.
And what have you done about that?

learn.vi: Nói bạn đã áp dụng họp giao việc hằng tuần và kết quả tốt hơn
learn.t: I introduced weekly planning meetings where tasks are assigned openly, and the team's output actually improved.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager.

learn.vi: Kể đã phản đối ra mắt sản phẩm sớm, đưa dữ liệu, được chấp nhận lùi hai tuần
learn.t: I once argued against launching a product early. I presented test data showing serious bugs, and we agreed to delay by two weeks.
Why should we choose you over the other candidates?

learn.vi: Nêu kinh nghiệm quản lý nhóm đa văn hoá và kết quả đo được
learn.t: I've led multicultural teams for six years and consistently delivered projects on time and under budget.

tests.t: Why are you leaving your current position?

tests.vi: Trả lời tích cực: tìm thử thách mới, không chê công ty cũ
tests.t: I've learned a great deal there, but I'm looking for a role with more strategic responsibility.
How do you handle a team member who consistently underperforms?

tests.vi: Nói sẽ nói chuyện riêng để tìm nguyên nhân, đặt mục tiêu rõ
tests.t: I'd speak to them privately to understand the cause, then agree clear goals and check progress regularly.
And if nothing improves?

tests.vi: Nói khi đó sẽ cùng phòng nhân sự xem xét các bước chính thức
tests.t: Then I'd involve HR and follow the formal procedure, while keeping the process fair and documented.

learn.t: The council has concerns about turning the car park into a community garden. Convince us.

learn.vi: Nêu lợi ích: không gian xanh, trẻ em có chỗ chơi, giảm nhiệt
learn.t: The garden would give families a green space, give children somewhere safe to play and help cool the neighbourhood.
But local shops depend on that parking.

learn.vi: Đề xuất giữ một nửa chỗ đỗ xe, chỉ chuyển một nửa thành vườn
learn.t: We could keep half the spaces for parking and convert only the other half.
And who would maintain it? We have no budget.

learn.vi: Nói cư dân sẽ tình nguyện chăm, đã có 60 người đăng ký
learn.t: Residents would maintain it as volunteers. Sixty people have already signed up.
Interesting. We'll consider a one-year trial.

learn.t: Thank you. We'd be happy to report back after six months.

tests.t: It would create a pedestrian street with a weekend market, and local businesses would attract more customers.
Residents worry about noise.

items.en: A Place You Like to Relax
items.p: Describe a place where you like to relax. Where is it? What do you do there? Why do you like it?
items.pv: Tả nơi bạn thích thư giãn: ở đâu, làm gì ở đó, vì sao thích.
c: Bạn đến đó khi nào / bao lâu một lần
u: One place I really like is
Một nơi tôi rất thích là
items.m: One place I really like is a small lake near my house. It's only ten minutes away by bike. I usually go there when I feel stressed after school or at the weekend. I sit on a bench, listen to music and watch people walking or fishing. Sometimes I take a book. What I like most is that it's quiet and green, even though it's in the middle of the city. It helps me forget about homework for a while, and I always feel calmer when I go home.

items.vi: Một điều hữu ích bạn đã học
items.p: Talk about something useful you learned outside school. Who taught you? How did you learn it? How has it helped you?
items.pv: Kể một điều hữu ích bạn học ngoài trường: ai dạy, học thế nào, giúp ích gì.
c: Ai dạy / học thế nào (quá khứ)
u: Một điều hữu ích tôi đã học là
At first it was difficult, but
items.m: Something useful I learned outside school was how to cook simple meals. My grandmother taught me when I stayed with her for a summer. At first it was difficult, because I kept burning the rice, but she was very patient and showed me again and again. Now I can cook several dishes, like fried rice, soup and fried eggs with tomatoes. It has helped me a lot, especially when my parents work late. I'm really glad she taught me, and I think everyone should learn to cook.

items.vi: Một dịp ăn mừng trong gia đình
items.p: Describe a family celebration you remember well. What was the occasion? Who was there? What happened?
items.pv: Kể một dịp ăn mừng gia đình bạn nhớ: dịp gì, ai có mặt, chuyện gì đã xảy ra.
c: Chuyện gì đã xảy ra (quá khứ)
u: Tôi sẽ không bao giờ quên
items.m: I remember my grandfather's eightieth birthday very well. It was two years ago, during the Tet holiday. The whole family came, more than thirty people, including cousins from Ho Chi Minh City I hadn't seen for years. We cooked together all morning and had a big lunch in the garden. The best moment was when my little cousins sang a song they had practised for weeks. My grandfather cried a little because he was so happy. I'll never forget that day, because it was the first time everyone was together.

items.vi: Kế hoạch năm tới của bạn
items.p: Talk about your plans for next year. What do you want to do? Why? What might make it difficult?
items.pv: Nói về kế hoạch năm tới: muốn làm gì, vì sao, điều gì có thể gây khó.
c: Bạn sẽ làm gì để vượt qua
u: The hardest part will probably be
Khó nhất có lẽ sẽ là
items.m: Next year I'm planning to take the IELTS exam and apply for a scholarship to study in Australia. The reason is that I want to study environmental science, and the best programmes are abroad. The hardest part will probably be the writing test, because I'm not very good at essays yet. Money could also be a problem if I don't get the scholarship. To deal with that, I'll practise writing every week with my teacher, and I'll also look for part-time work so I can save some money.

items.vi: Mua hàng online hay ở cửa hàng
items.p: Do you prefer shopping online or in shops? Talk about the advantages and disadvantages, and give your opinion.
items.pv: Bạn thích mua online hay ở cửa hàng? Nói ưu, nhược điểm và ý kiến của bạn.
items.m: Personally, I prefer shopping online for most things. One advantage is that it saves a lot of time, because I don't have to travel or queue. It's also easy to compare prices. The problem is that you can't touch or try things before you buy them. I once bought a jacket online that was much too small, and returning it was really annoying. For clothes and shoes, I still prefer going to shops. Overall, I think online shopping is better for things like books and electronics, but shops are better when the size or quality really matters.

items.p: Talk about a person who helped you when you needed it. Who were they? What did they do? How did you feel?
items.pv: Kể về một người đã giúp bạn lúc cần: là ai, đã làm gì, bạn cảm thấy thế nào.
u: I was having a hard time because
Tôi đang gặp khó khăn vì
Cô ấy giúp tôi bằng cách
items.m: I'd like to talk about my maths teacher in grade ten, Ms Lan. I was having a hard time because my parents were getting divorced, and my marks were falling. She noticed that I was quiet in class and asked me to stay after a lesson. She didn't ask too many questions, but she offered to help me with maths for free twice a week. She also told me I could talk to her any time. I felt really grateful, because I didn't feel alone anymore. My marks improved, and we still send each other messages at Tet.

items.vi: Một thay đổi ở nơi bạn sống
items.p: Describe an important change in your town or neighbourhood in recent years. What changed? How has it affected people? Is it a positive change overall?
items.pv: Tả một thay đổi quan trọng ở nơi bạn sống gần đây: thay đổi gì, ảnh hưởng ra sao, nhìn chung có tích cực không.
items.m: Over the past few years, the biggest change in my neighbourhood has been the opening of a new metro line. Before that, getting to the city centre could take over an hour in traffic. On the plus side, people can now commute much faster, and the air near the main road seems a little cleaner because fewer people use motorbikes. Small businesses near the stations have also become busier. The downside is that rents have gone up a lot, and some older families have had to move further out. The construction also caused years of noise and dust. All things considered, I think it's a positive change, but the city should do more to protect people who can't afford higher rents.

items.vi: Bài học từ một sai lầm
items.p: Tell me about a mistake you made and what you learned from it. What happened? Why did it happen? What would you do differently now?
items.pv: Kể một sai lầm và bài học: chuyện gì, vì sao, giờ bạn sẽ làm khác thế nào.
c: Bài học / giờ sẽ làm khác
u: One mistake I'll never forget is
Một sai lầm tôi không quên là
If I could do it again, I'd
Nếu được làm lại, tôi sẽ
items.m: One mistake I'll never forget is when I agreed to lead three group projects at university in the same term. I wanted to look responsible, and I didn't want to say no to my friends. Looking back, the reason was that I didn't think realistically about how much time each project would take. As a result, I was exhausted, all three projects were finished at the last minute, and one of them got a really poor mark, which affected my whole group. If I could do it again, I'd only take on one leadership role and be honest about my limits. I've learned that saying no politely is much better than letting people down later.

items.vi: Người trẻ có nên đi du lịch một mình?
items.p: Some people think young people should travel alone at least once. Do you agree? Talk about the benefits and the risks, and give your opinion.
items.pv: Có người cho rằng người trẻ nên đi du lịch một mình ít nhất một lần. Bạn đồng ý không? Nói lợi ích, rủi ro và ý kiến.
u: Dù vậy, có những rủi ro
items.m: I'm inclined to agree, as long as it's done sensibly. Travelling alone forces you to make your own decisions, solve problems and talk to strangers, which builds confidence in a way that's hard to get at home. When I travelled alone to Da Lat for a week, I had to deal with a cancelled bus and a hostel that had lost my booking, and I came back feeling much more independent. That said, there are risks. Young people may be less aware of scams or unsafe areas, and if something goes wrong, there's nobody to help immediately. So I'd say it's a great experience, but people should start with a safe destination, tell their family their plans and keep some emergency money.

items.vi: Một sở thích tốn thời gian
items.p: Describe a hobby or activity that you have spent a lot of time on. How did you start? What do you enjoy about it? Has it changed you in any way?
items.pv: Tả một sở thích bạn dành nhiều thời gian: bắt đầu thế nào, thích điều gì, nó có thay đổi bạn không.
c: Nó thay đổi bạn ra sao
u: Điều khiến tôi thấy đáng là
items.m: I've been playing the guitar for about six years now. I got into it when my older cousin left his old guitar at our house and never came back for it. At first I just watched online videos and practised a few simple songs, but after a while I joined a small band with some friends from school. What I find rewarding is that progress is very clear: a song that seemed impossible a month ago suddenly becomes easy. Playing with other people is also great fun. It has taught me patience and discipline, because there are no shortcuts, you just have to practise. It has also made me more confident performing in front of people.

items.en: The Role of Technology in Education
items.vi: Vai trò của công nghệ trong giáo dục
items.p: How has technology changed the way people learn? Talk about the advantages and disadvantages and say whether you think schools use technology well.
items.pv: Công nghệ đã thay đổi cách học thế nào? Nói ưu, nhược và liệu trường học có dùng công nghệ tốt không.
c: Công nghệ thay đổi cách học thế nào
u: Công nghệ đã thay đổi hoàn toàn
items.m: Technology has completely changed the way people learn. Twenty years ago, if you wanted to learn something, you needed a teacher or a library. Now you can find videos, courses and practice exercises on almost any subject for free. The main advantage is access: students in small towns can learn from excellent teachers anywhere in the world. On the other hand, it's very easy to get distracted, and some students just copy answers from the internet without really understanding them. In my experience, schools don't always use technology well. Some teachers just put their slides online, which doesn't really change anything. I think technology works best when it's used for practice and feedback, not as a replacement for good teaching.

items.p: Tell me about a time you had to have a difficult conversation with someone. What was it about? How did you handle it? What was the result?
items.pv: Kể lần bạn phải nói chuyện khó với ai đó: về chuyện gì, bạn xử lý thế nào, kết quả ra sao.
items.m: A few months ago I had to tell my best friend that I couldn't lend her any more money. She had borrowed money from me several times and hadn't paid it back, and it was starting to affect our friendship. It was difficult because I didn't want to hurt her or make her feel embarrassed. I tried to choose a calm moment, when we were having coffee, and I explained honestly that I was struggling with money myself. I didn't blame her. In the end, she was actually relieved that I had said something, and she apologised. She has paid back most of it now, and our friendship is stronger because we were honest with each other.

items.p: Some people say that failure is more valuable than success. To what extent do you agree? Use examples from your own experience or from society.
items.pv: Có người nói thất bại quý hơn thành công. Bạn đồng ý tới mức nào? Dùng ví dụ từ bản thân hoặc xã hội.
c: Lý lẽ ủng hộ có ví dụ
u: I'd agree up to a point
Tôi đồng ý ở một mức độ
That said, it would be naive to
Dù vậy, thật ngây thơ nếu
Điều thật sự quan trọng là
items.m: I'd agree up to a point. Failure tends to teach us things that success rarely does, because it forces us to analyse what went wrong. When I failed my first driving test, I realised I'd been relying on luck rather than practice, and that changed how I prepare for anything important. In business, too, many successful founders say their first company failed and that they learned more from it than from any course. That said, it would be naive to romanticise failure. Repeated failure can destroy confidence, and not everyone can afford to fail: someone who loses their savings on a failed business may never get a second chance. So what really matters is not failure itself but the conditions around it: whether people have the support and security to reflect on it and try again. Without that, failure is just painful.

items.vi: Cân bằng công việc và cuộc sống
items.p: Many people find it hard to balance work and personal life. Why do you think this is? Whose responsibility is it to improve the situation: individuals, employers or governments?
items.pv: Nhiều người khó cân bằng công việc và đời sống. Vì sao? Trách nhiệm cải thiện thuộc về cá nhân, công ty hay nhà nước?
c: Vai trò của công ty / nhà nước
u: There are several reasons for this
Ở mức nào đó, cá nhân có thể
Tuy nhiên, thật khó kỳ vọng
items.m: There are several reasons for this. Technology means work can follow us everywhere, so the boundary between the office and home has almost disappeared. Many jobs are also less secure than in the past, so people feel they have to be constantly available to keep their position. To some extent, individuals can protect themselves, for example by switching off notifications in the evening or being clear about their limits. However, it's unrealistic to expect people to do this alone if their manager sends messages at eleven at night and expects an answer. Employers set the culture, so they have a big responsibility. Governments can help too: some countries now give workers a legal right to disconnect after working hours. Ultimately, I'd argue that the main responsibility lies with employers, because individual effort rarely changes a culture that rewards overwork.

items.en: A Decision That Shaped Your Life
items.vi: Một quyết định định hình cuộc đời bạn
items.p: Describe a decision that had a significant effect on your life. What were the options? How did you decide? Would you make the same choice again?
items.pv: Tả một quyết định ảnh hưởng lớn tới đời bạn: có những lựa chọn nào, bạn quyết định ra sao, có chọn lại như thế không.
c: Hoàn cảnh và các lựa chọn
Có chọn lại như thế không
items.m: The decision that shaped my life most was choosing to study linguistics instead of medicine. My family had always assumed I would become a doctor, and I had good enough grades. I was torn between meeting their expectations and following my genuine interest in languages. What tipped the balance was a conversation with a doctor friend of my father's, who told me honestly that medicine is too demanding to do without real passion. I chose linguistics, and my parents were disappointed for a while. It turned out to be the right choice: I now work as a translator and I genuinely enjoy my work, which I don't think I would have done in a hospital. With hindsight, I'd make the same decision, though I'd explain my reasons to my parents earlier and more clearly.

items.en: Should Cities Ban Cars from Centres?
items.vi: Thành phố có nên cấm ô tô ở trung tâm?
items.p: Some cities have banned private cars from their centres. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this policy and say whether it would work in a city you know.
items.pv: Một số thành phố cấm xe riêng ở trung tâm. Bàn ưu, nhược và liệu chính sách này có hợp với thành phố bạn biết không.
c: Áp dụng vào thành phố bạn biết
items.m: The most obvious benefit is cleaner air and safer streets. When cars are removed, city centres become quieter and more pleasant, and in several European cities, shops actually reported more customers because people spent longer walking around. Critics point out, however, that a ban can be unfair to people with disabilities, older residents and businesses that depend on deliveries. It can also simply push traffic into surrounding neighbourhoods. In the case of Hanoi, I think a complete ban would be difficult right now, because most people use motorbikes and public transport is still being developed. A gradual approach might work better, starting with car-free weekends around Hoan Kiem Lake, which have already been popular. So it would only work if public transport is reliable and there are exceptions for people who genuinely need vehicles.

items.vi: Ảnh hưởng của người nổi tiếng
items.p: How much influence do celebrities and influencers have on young people today? Is this influence mainly positive or negative? Give reasons and examples.
items.pv: Người nổi tiếng và người có ảnh hưởng tác động tới giới trẻ thế nào? Chủ yếu tích cực hay tiêu cực? Nêu lý do và ví dụ.
c: Ảnh hưởng tích cực có ví dụ
Ảnh hưởng tiêu cực có ví dụ
items.m: It's hard to overstate how much influence they have. Many young people spend hours a day watching influencers, and they often trust them more than traditional media. To be fair, some of that influence is positive. Several Vietnamese creators have encouraged young people to read more, learn languages or talk openly about mental health, which was a taboo subject not long ago. The darker side is the pressure to look and live in a certain way. Constant images of perfect bodies and expensive lifestyles can make teenagers feel inadequate, and some influencers promote products they clearly know nothing about. On the whole, I'd say the influence is mixed, and what matters most is whether young people learn to think critically about what they watch, which is something schools could teach far more effectively.

items.vi: Một truyền thống đáng giữ gìn
items.p: Describe a tradition in your country that you think should be preserved. What does it involve? Why is it important? What threatens it?
items.pv: Tả một truyền thống ở nước bạn nên được giữ: gồm những gì, vì sao quan trọng, điều gì đe doạ nó.
u: A tradition I value deeply is
Một truyền thống tôi rất trân trọng là
Điều làm nó đặc biệt là
Đáng buồn, nó đang bị đe doạ bởi
One way to keep it alive
items.m: A tradition I value deeply is the family meal on the first day of Tet, when several generations gather at the oldest relative's house. It involves preparing traditional dishes like banh chung, offering food at the family altar and then eating together for hours. What makes it special is that it connects people to their ancestors and to each other, and it's often the only time the whole extended family is in one place. Sadly, it's under threat from busy modern lives. More families now travel during Tet or order food instead of cooking together, and younger people sometimes see it as an obligation rather than something meaningful. One way to keep it alive might be to adapt it rather than insist on every detail, for example sharing the cooking so it isn't a burden for one person, which is usually a woman.

items.vi: Quyền riêng tư có đang lỗi thời?
items.p: Some argue that privacy is becoming an outdated idea in a connected world. Do you agree? Discuss the implications for individuals and society.
items.pv: Có người cho rằng quyền riêng tư đang lỗi thời trong thế giới kết nối. Bạn đồng ý không? Bàn tác động tới cá nhân và xã hội.
c: Lập luận kết, có sắc thái
u: Tôi không đồng tình điểm đó
Điều đã thay đổi không phải là
items.m: I'd take issue with that claim. What has changed is not the value of privacy but how much effort it takes to protect it. People share a great deal online, but that doesn't mean they've stopped caring; surveys consistently show that most people are uneasy about how their data is collected, they simply feel powerless to do anything about it. For individuals, the loss of privacy can be very concrete: personal information can be used to manipulate purchases, raise insurance prices or expose people to harassment. The implications go well beyond individuals, though. Privacy is what allows people to explore ideas, form opinions and organise without constant observation, and a society in which everyone assumes they are being watched tends to become more cautious and conformist. If anything, I'd argue that privacy matters more than ever precisely because it's so easily lost, and that the burden of protecting it should shift from individuals to the companies and governments that collect the data.

items.vi: Mục đích của giáo dục đại học
items.p: What do you think the main purpose of university education should be: preparing people for jobs, or developing the ability to think independently? Can it do both?
items.pv: Mục đích chính của đại học nên là chuẩn bị đi làm hay phát triển tư duy độc lập? Có thể làm được cả hai không?
c: Hai quan niệm về mục đích
Lý lẽ cho định hướng nghề nghiệp
Lý lẽ cho tư duy độc lập
Có thể kết hợp không, ra sao
u: Vấn đề thường được đặt thành
Yet it would be short-sighted to
Thế nhưng thật thiển cận nếu
The two are far from incompatible
Hai điều này hoàn toàn không mâu thuẫn
items.m: This is often framed as a choice between two opposing goals, but I think that's a false dichotomy. There's a strong case for vocational relevance: students and their families invest enormous amounts of money and time, and it's reasonable for them to expect degrees that lead to decent employment. Universities that ignore the labour market risk producing graduates who struggle to find work. Yet it would be short-sighted to reduce education to job training. Many of the jobs today's students will do don't exist yet, and the skills that last, such as analysing evidence, writing clearly and questioning assumptions, are exactly those developed by a broad, rigorous education. The two are far from incompatible. The best programmes I've encountered combine practical projects with genuine intellectual challenge, so that students learn to apply knowledge while also learning to doubt it. If universities have to prioritise, though, I'd lean towards independent thinking, since specific technical skills date quickly while the ability to learn does not.

items.p: Describe a work of art, music or literature that affected you deeply. What is it? Why did it have such an impact on you? Has your view of it changed over time?

u: One work that has stayed with me is
Một tác phẩm vẫn ở mãi trong tôi là
What struck me at the time was
Điều làm tôi ấn tượng lúc đó là
Đọc / xem lại nhiều năm sau,
items.m: One work that has stayed with me is Bao Ninh's novel The Sorrow of War, which I first read at about seventeen. What struck me at the time was how completely it contradicted the heroic stories of the war I had grown up with. The narrator is haunted, confused and often unable to make sense of what he has lived through, and the book moves back and forth in time in a way that mirrors his memory. I read it during a period when my grandfather, who had fought in the war, rarely spoke about it, and the book helped me understand his silence. Revisiting it years later, I noticed things I had missed: the love story, which I had found almost secondary, now seemed central, a picture of everything the war destroyed. It taught me that literature can tell truths that official histories leave out, and that a single honest voice can be more powerful than a thousand slogans.

items.vi: Ngôn ngữ toàn cầu và ngôn ngữ địa phương
items.p: As English and a few other languages spread worldwide, many smaller languages are disappearing. Does this matter? What, if anything, should be done?
items.pv: Khi tiếng Anh và vài ngôn ngữ lớn lan rộng, nhiều ngôn ngữ nhỏ biến mất. Điều này có đáng lo không? Nên làm gì?
c: Có đáng lo không, vì sao
Mặt lợi của ngôn ngữ toàn cầu
Mất mát khi ngôn ngữ nhỏ biến mất
u: It matters a great deal, in my view
Theo tôi, điều này rất quan trọng
Khi một ngôn ngữ biến mất,
Thay vì chống lại tiếng Anh,
items.m: It matters a great deal, in my view, although the issue is more complicated than it first appears. Admittedly, global languages bring real benefits. A shared language allows scientists to collaborate, opens up educational opportunities and gives speakers of small languages access to a much wider world, so it's understandable that parents want their children to learn English. When a language disappears, however, something irreplaceable is lost: ways of describing nature, family relationships and humour that exist nowhere else, as well as oral histories that were never written down. In Vietnam, several ethnic minority languages have very few young speakers left. What should be done is not to discourage people from learning global languages but to support bilingualism, for example through early schooling in the mother tongue, recordings of elderly speakers and media in local languages. Rather than resisting English, communities need the resources to keep their own languages alive alongside it.

items.p: Are there questions that science cannot answer? Discuss with reference to areas such as ethics, art or human experience.
items.pv: Có câu hỏi nào khoa học không trả lời được? Bàn với các lĩnh vực như đạo đức, nghệ thuật hay trải nghiệm con người.
c: Ví dụ: nghệ thuật / trải nghiệm
u: It depends partly on what we mean by
Phần nào tuỳ vào ta hiểu thế nào là
Lấy đạo đức làm ví dụ
Điều tương tự cũng đúng với
items.m: It depends partly on what we mean by an answer, but I'd say yes, there are important questions science can't settle on its own. Take ethics, for instance. Science can tell us what the consequences of a policy are likely to be, how many lives a vaccine will save or how much a new road will increase pollution, but it cannot tell us how to weigh those consequences against each other or what we owe to future generations. Those are questions of values. The same is true of art. Neuroscience can describe what happens in the brain when we listen to music, but that description doesn't explain why a particular piece feels meaningful, or whether it is good. And there's the question of subjective experience itself: what it is like to be in love or to grieve. None of this diminishes science, which remains our most reliable way of understanding the physical world. It simply suggests that a complete understanding of human life needs philosophy, art and personal reflection as well.

items.vi: Tham vọng và sự hài lòng
items.p: Is ambition always a good thing? Discuss the relationship between ambition and personal happiness, drawing on examples.
items.pv: Tham vọng có luôn tốt? Bàn mối liên hệ giữa tham vọng và hạnh phúc cá nhân, có ví dụ.
c: Mặt tích cực của tham vọng
Cân bằng giữa tham vọng và hài lòng
u: Tham vọng thường được coi là
Perhaps the healthiest form of ambition
Có lẽ dạng tham vọng lành mạnh nhất
items.m: Ambition is often treated as an unquestionable virtue, but I don't think it's always a good thing. Without it, of course, very little would be achieved; many of the people who have improved our lives, from scientists to social reformers, were driven by a powerful desire to accomplish something. On a personal level, having goals gives structure and meaning to daily life. Taken too far, however, ambition can become a source of permanent dissatisfaction. If your sense of worth depends on the next promotion or achievement, every success is quickly replaced by a new target, and there's never a moment to enjoy what you already have. I've seen colleagues earn excellent salaries and still feel like failures because someone else had done better. Perhaps the healthiest form of ambition is directed towards doing something well, or contributing to something larger, rather than towards status. That kind of ambition can coexist with contentment, because its rewards come from the work itself rather than from comparison with others.
